content: 1. Lamivudine and raltegravir are indicated for use in combination with other antiretroviral agents for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults and pediatric patients aged 6 years or older, weighing at least 30 kg. The recommended dosage is one tablet (150 mg/300 mg) taken orally twice daily. The safety and efficacy of this combination have not been established in children under 6 years of age. 2. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of raltegravir by binding cations in the gastrointestinal tract. This combination is contraindicated and not recommended, even with dose separation. 3. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of raltegravir by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The combination is contraindicated and not recommended, even with dose separation. 4. Aluminum hydroxide/magnesium trisilicate also decreases the levels or effects of raltegravir by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The combination is contraindicated and not recommended, even with dose separation. 5. Lamivudine and emtricitabine-containing products should not be coadministered due to the risk of therapeutic duplication and increased risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Magnesium supplements decrease the levels or effects of raltegravir by forming chelates with polyvalent cations, reducing absorption in the gastrointestinal tract. This interaction applies to oral forms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Sorbitol-containing solutions decrease the systemic exposure of lamivudine oral solution, as shown in pediatric studies (e.g., the ARROW trial). This results in lower rates of virologic suppression, reduced plasma lamivudine exposure, and increased viral resistance compared to children receiving lamivudine tablets. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Tafenoquine increases the levels or effects of lamivudine by inhibiting organic cation transporter-2 (OCT2) and multidrug and toxin extrusion (MATE) transporters in vitro. Avoid coadministration with OCT2 or MATE substrates. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for substrate-related toxicities and consider dosage adjustments based on product labeling. 9. Abacavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of raltegravir by increasing its elimination. Apalutamide induces UGT enzymes, which may reduce the systemic exposure of drugs that are UGT substrates. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Atazanavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Antiretroviral medications, including lamivudine and raltegravir, may interfere with the manufacturing of autologous cell-based therapies such as atidarsagene autotemcel, betibeglogene autotemcel, and lovotibeglogene autotemcel. Patients should discontinue antiretroviral therapy for at least one month before cell mobilization or the expected duration for drug elimination and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Some long-acting antiretroviral agents may require a longer discontinuation period. 13. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of raltegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Magnesium-containing antacids reduce raltegravir plasma levels when taken within six hours of the raltegravir dose. 14. Ganciclovir and lamivudine increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of hematologic toxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 15. Peginterferon alfa-2a or alfa-2b and lamivudine increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of liver decompensation. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Rifampin decreases the levels of raltegravir by increasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Ritonavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Selenium decreases the levels or effects of raltegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer raltegravir at least two hours before or six hours after polyvalent cation-containing products. Note that dose separation may not adequately avoid this interaction. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 19. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate increases the levels or effects of raltegravir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Administer drugs at least two hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 20. Lamivudine and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Tipranavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Trimethoprim increases the effects of lamivudine by competing for renal tubular clearance. This may lead to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Ublituximab decreases the effects of raltegravir and lamivudine through immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 24. Valganciclovir and lamivudine increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of hematologic toxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 25. Zinc decreases the levels or effects of raltegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer raltegravir two hours before or six hours after polyvalent cation-containing products. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 26. Isavuconazonium sulfate, an OCT2 inhibitor, may increase the effects or levels of lamivudine. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor closely. 27. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of lamivudine by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor closely. 28. Lamivudine increases the effects of zidovudine through pharmacodynamic synergism, which may be beneficial. Monitor closely.
